name: yosys
why: Open-source Verilog synthesis lets you turn hardware descriptions into real netlists, a genuine door into circuit design.

brief.what_it_is: Yosys is a framework for Verilog RTL synthesis, driven from a command-line binary with an interactive shell or from synthesis scripts. It takes Verilog-2005 designs, and per the GitHub README also an informally defined synthesizable subset of SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800-2017 or 2023), via the sv-elab and slang libraries. It outputs gate-level netlists mapped to ASIC standard cell libraries in Liberty format or to Xilinx 7-Series, Lattice iCE40 and ECP5 FPGAs, and it can also convert designs to BLIF, EDIF, BTOR, SMT-LIB or simple RTL Verilog. It has built-in formal methods for property and equivalence checking.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Yosys as a foundation and front-end for custom flows: "Yosys can be adapted to perform any synthesis job by combining the existing passes (algorithms) using synthesis scripts and adding additional passes as needed by extending the Yosys C++ code base." It also serves as the backend for formal tools such as sby and mcy.
brief.how_it_works: You chain named passes in a script or the interactive shell. Typical steps are read_verilog, hierarchy -top, proc and opt to turn always blocks into netlist elements, techmap to map to the internal cell library, dfflibmap -liberty for flip-flops, abc -liberty for combinational logic, then write_verilog. The synth command bundles a good default script that you can build on.

brief.install_notes: The Homebrew formula's caveats are empty. The README's easiest route is a binary suite: the free OSS CAD Suite from github.com/YosysHQ/oss-cad-suite-build releases (includes all dependencies and related tools), or the commercial Tabby CAD Suite, which needs a YosysHQ evaluation license. Many Linux distributions package Yosys too, though versions vary. Building from source needs many packages, CMake, git submodules (--recurse-submodules), and a C++ toolchain; release builds use cmake --preset release. Building the docs additionally needs Sphinx, pdf2svg, faketime and a LaTeX install. No first-run configuration beyond running the binary was described.
brief.standout: Yosys is a scriptable pipeline of named passes rather than a fixed black-box tool, and it is extensible in C++, so you can build custom flows. Formal property and equivalence checking is built in, and it doubles as the synthesis backend for other formal tools such as sby and mcy.
brief.status: Appears maintained, but I could not confirm a date. I did not see a release date or last-commit date in the pages I read. The README references recent work, including IEEE 1800-2023 SystemVerilog support, CMake presets, and a commercial vendor (YosysHQ) that sells the Tabby CAD Suite, plus a blog and a Discourse forum. Status is therefore probably active, but not verified from commit or release data.
brief.caveats: read_verilog does no syntax checking, so the README suggests linting with Verilator first. SystemVerilog support is for an informally defined synthesizable subset, and industry-grade SystemVerilog and VHDL parsers are gated behind the commercial Tabby CAD Suite evaluation license. Building from source has a heavy dependency list and needs submodules. Linux distro packages may lag. Licensed under ISC, which the README says is GPL-compatible; third-party code in the abc and libs subdirectories has its own licence terms. The brew caveats field is empty.
